questions.question_text: Round a census count of $176\,248$ to the nearest hundred.

options.why: Rounded up even though the tens digit is $4$, which requires rounding down.
Rounded to the nearest ten instead of the nearest hundred requested.
Rounded to the nearest thousand instead of the nearest hundred.

questions.question_text: Round the measured distance $3\,458\,620$ m to the nearest thousand metres.

options.why: Truncated the hundreds, tens and ones instead of using the hundreds digit to round up.
Rounded to the nearest ten thousand rather than to the nearest thousand metres.
Rounded to the nearest hundred metres instead of the nearest thousand metres.

questions.question_text: Round $67\,944\,100$ to the nearest ten thousand.

options.why: Rounded the ten-thousands digit up even though the thousands digit is only $4$.
Rounded to the nearest thousand rather than replacing four lower digits with zeros.
Rounded to the nearest hundred thousand instead of the nearest ten thousand.

questions.question_text: A regional estimate is $418\,750\,000$. Round it to the nearest hundred thousand.

options.why: Rounded down at the halfway digit $5$ instead of applying the round-up rule.
Rounded to the nearest million rather than the nearest hundred thousand.
Left the original value unchanged instead of replacing the lower five digits with zeros.

questions.question_text: Round the reported population $92\,499\,999$ to the nearest million.

options.why: Rounded up even though $499\,999$ is below the halfway point of $500\,000$.
Rounded to the nearest hundred thousand instead of the nearest million.
Rounded to the nearest ten million rather than the nearest million.

questions.question_text: $7\,263\,850$ was rounded to $7\,264\,000$. To which place was it rounded?

options.why: Focused on the hundreds digit used to decide, rather than the thousands digit being rounded.
Counted one zero too many; rounding to ten thousand would give $7\,260\,000$.
Used the largest period name instead of inspecting which lower digits became zero.

questions.solution_text:
The hundreds digit $8$ rounded the thousands digit up.
It was rounded to the nearest thousand.

questions.question_text: A whole-number census count rounds to $3\,600\,000$ to the nearest hundred thousand. What is the smallest possible count?

options.why: Used the lower hundred-thousand mark instead of the halfway value that first rounds up.
Chose a value just below the rounded result rather than the smallest value in its rounding interval.
Used the upper halfway boundary, which rounds to $3\,700\,000$ rather than $3\,600\,000$.

questions.solution_text:
The halfway point below $3\,600\,000$ is $3\,550\,000$.
Smallest possible count $=3\,550\,000$

questions.question_text: A whole-number distance rounds to $81\,000$ m to the nearest thousand metres. What is the largest possible distance?

options.why: Used the upper halfway boundary, which rounds up to $82\,000$ m.
Used the end of the next thousand instead of the end of the interval centred on $81\,000$ m.
Chose a value below the rounded result rather than the greatest value that rounds to it.

questions.solution_text:
$81\,500$ m rounds up to $82\,000$ m.
Largest possible distance $=81\,499$ m
